sources.researchNote: The upload title gives 1927 without distinguishing the composition, recording or issue. sources.fullCitation: Ilja Livschakoff et son Orchestre. “Une chanson de mon pays.” Slowfox from Mélodie d’amour; label credit “Kaper–Jurmann–Rotter”. Polydor 24604, label number A 24604. Disc label shown in the YouTube transfer published by Ilja Livschakoff.
sources.title: Une chanson de mon pays — Polydor 24604
sources.creator: Ilja Livschakoff et son Orchestre
sources.researchNote: The label shown identifies the French title “Une chanson de mon pays”, the film Mélodie d’amour, Ilja Livschakoff et son Orchestre, Polydor 24604 and the printed number A 24604. The uploader gives the German title “Ein Lied aus meiner Heimat”, matrix 4735 BD VII and a Berlin session around May 1932. The matrix and approximate recording date are not visible on the label; the date is not an established issue date. The separate Rosvaenge/Livschakoff master 4733 ½ BD is not evidence for this transfer’s matrix.

sources.shortCitation: Polydor 47019 B, Lys Gauty, “Le bistro du port”
sources.fullCitation: Lys Gauty, with orchestra. “Le bistro du port” (In der Hafenschänke). Polydor 47019 B, n.d. Disc-label photograph and audio transfer uploaded by Jan Bus114 to Internet Archive, 31 July 2024.
sources.title: Le bistro du port — Lys Gauty, Polydor 47019 B
sources.creator: Lys Gauty; Jan Bus114 (uploader)
sources.researchNote: The photographed label identifies Polydor 47019 B, Lys Gauty with orchestral accompaniment, and the credit Candel–Groener–Saudmont; it does not name the orchestra or conductor. The uploader associates the transfer with Polydor 47019 or 522987 and gives matrix 1444 1/2 WPP; that matrix is not independently transcribed from the photograph. The item gives 1933 and asks ‘Paris 1933?’; these do not establish the session or issue date. Frémeaux & Associés’ discography (SRC0884) identifies the Gauty recording as Polydor 522987, matrix 1444 WPP, recorded in Paris on 18 October 1934. The relation of the matrix notation and the exact take of this transfer remain unverified. The structured date is the Internet Archive upload date, not the date of the historical disc.

works.title: Le bistrot du port
works.publicNote: Valse written for the singer Lys Gauty, to words by Gaston Groener and A. Saudemont; the printed edition (Paris: Coda, cop. 1934) credits the music to Pierre Candel, a pseudonym standing here for Kaper and Jurmann together. In his 1975 AFI oral history Kaper recalled it as the last song he wrote in Paris, and said he never heard it there before leaving for the United States.
